names.__title: RC — sprint analysis vs the professional model

Key positions vs professionals (flying s: White = the world-class 100 m average (published mean angles, Bissas 2022 / Clark 2025), drawn with RC's own segment lengths and anchored at his stance foot. Left: touchdown, left foot landing; his right (red) swing knee is behind and the shin points back, while the white swing knee is through and the heel tucked under (figure 4). Middle: toe-off; his push-off leg is straight, the white one still bent. Right: touchdown on the ← run, left leg swinging.
The five key positions, flying sprint →. Top row: right foot lands (near). Bottom row: left foot lands, right (red) leg swinging. Thin line = vertical through the hips.
Arm action (near-side arm, flying sprint: Right arm at the front and the back of one swing (flying sprint →). In front the upper arm only reaches the side of the trunk (hand at mid-chest); at the back it swings well behind with the elbow opening.
Timing and stride (near-side leg, mean ±: Every step of the four runs. Filled = near-side leg (high confidence), hollow = far side.

names.__title: Vinni — mile pace and kick vs the professional model, plus backflip

Key positions vs professionals: White = the world-class sprinter average (Bissas 2022 / Clark 2025), drawn with his segment lengths and anchored at his stance foot; it shows direction at mile pace and applies to the kick. Left: mile-pace touchdown, left foot landing; his right (red) swing leg trails far behind. Middle: mile-pace toe-off, push-off leg straight. Right: kick touchdown, the same pattern.
The key positions at mile pace (→ run). Top row: right foot lands. Bottom row: left foot lands, right (red) leg swinging. Thin line = vertical through the hips.
Timing and stride (near-side leg, mean ±: Every step of the four runs. Filled = near-side leg, hollow = far side.
Backflip critique (extra): Backflip key frames with tracked skeleton; time is from toe-off.
Shaded = flight. The trunk stops rotating at about 52° while he rises (stall), the tuck starts at the top, and he lands at 266° of the 360° needed.
